entries.proposition: The case and control groups differ enormously in exposure (betel-quid chewing 80 against 17 percent, smoking 88 against 53 percent), cases come from two hospitals and controls from a biobank, and the ORs are from models adjusted for these.
entries.snippet: Significant differences were observed in the distribution of betel-quid chewing (p < 0.001), cigarette smoking (p < 0.001), and alcohol consumption (p < 0.001) between the controls and patients with OSCC.
entries.anchor: Results, Association between WWOX single nucleotide polymorphisms and OSCC

entries.proposition: The risk association is modest and is carried by the TT genotype (55 cases, 52 controls); the heterozygotes show no association.
entries.snippet: oral cancer patients with the WWOX polymorphic rs11545028 T/T and combination of CT and TT genotypes exhibited a 1.824-fold (95% CI: 1.224-2.716) and 1.227-fold (95% CI: 1.022-1.473; both p < 0.05) higher risk of OSCC than did patients with the corresponding WT homozygous gene.

entries.proposition: The variant is called a 'nonsense polymorphism in exon 1' in the Discussion, a 5'UTR variant in Table 1 and a Kozak-context variant elsewhere; a 5'UTR C>T change cannot be a nonsense change.
entries.snippet: Notably, we observed that the nonsense polymorphism rs11545028 C > T located in exon 1 conferred an increased risk of OSCC.

entries.proposition: The reporter used to support a translational (Kozak) mechanism is described only as a promoter-region construct in a pGL3-Enhancer vector (the insert boundaries are not given); the paper itself infers 'translational initiation' from the lower luciferase of the T allele. That such a construct reports transcriptional output rather than translation initiation is my inference, not the paper's statement.
entries.snippet: A luciferase reporter plasmid encompassing the major allele (C) and minor allele (T) of rs11545028 in the promoter region of the WWOX gene was cloned into the pGL3-Enhancer Luciferase Reporter Vectors (Promega Corp., Madison, WI, USA), according to manufacturer instructions.

entries.proposition: The conclusion that the T allele lowers translation initiation rests on the mRNA and IHC associations and the reporter, none of which measures translation; the mRNA is lower, which a transcriptional or stability effect would also give.
entries.snippet: Overall, our findings suggest that the rs11545028 T allele reduced the translation initiation rate, which subsequently reduced the WWOX expression, thus contributing to a more aggressive phenotype in OSCC.

entries.snippet: We found that OSCC patient who carry C/T or T/T of rs11545028 polymorphism have significantly lower mRNA levels of WWOX compare to C/C genotype (Figure 2B).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 2: relative luciferase activity of the T-allele construct is about 0.65 (HSC-3), about 0.08 (OECM-1) and about 0.68 (SCC-9) of the C allele, a roughly ten-fold fall in one line against about one-third in two; tumour WWOX mRNA is lower in C/T or T/T than C/C (P = 0.042, about 19 and 15 points); IHC weak/strong counts are C/C 11 and 22, C/T or T/T 12 and 6 with percentages that are column percentages (P = 0.022; a Fisher exact test on the same counts gives about 0.038, my own arithmetic).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2A bar chart rs11545028 C allele white and T allele blue in HSC-3, OECM-1, SCC-9; 2B dot plot relative WWOX mRNA levels C/C against C/T or T/T P=0.042; 2C and 2D IHC weak and strong fields; 2E table weak 11 (47.8%) and 12 (52.2%), strong 22 (78.6%) and 6 (21.4%), p 0.022.
